Revised assessment using the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) as reference:

- The FOMC statement highlights improved market functioning and strong policy accommodation, but SLOOS (July 2020) shows broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms across C&I (for firms of all sizes), CRE, and consumer credit, reflecting reduced risk tolerance and concerns about collateral values and the economic outlook.
- Banks reported weaker demand for C&I and CRE loans, and expected to tighten standards further over the remainder of 2020 amid anticipated deterioration in credit quality, especially in CRE and credit cards. This signals headwinds for the “flow of credit to households and businesses” despite policy support.
- Mortgage demand was solid in some categories (notably refis and GSE/government-backed) due to low rates, partially offsetting weakness, but standards generally tightened there as well.
- Net read: Relative to a headline FOMC read, SLOOS indicates constrained bank intermediation and prospective further tightening, reinforcing downside risks to activity and employment.
